TITLE: Arista Q3 2026: AI and campus lift next year’s estimates
QUOTE: Our first look at 2027 guidance range puts us in the 38%–40% range for growth annually to approximately $18.5 billion.
QUOTE_WHO: Jayshree Ullal, Chairperson and CEO, Q3 2026 earnings call, 3 November 2026
COMPANY_INTRO: Arista Networks sells Ethernet switches, routers and EOS software to cloud operators, AI data centres and enterprises. Products are 87% of revenue; 2026 revenue is guided at $13.3bn. Listed on the NYSE, market value about $214bn.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Beat
TAKEAWAYS.text: Revenue 9.7% above consensus and EPS 11% above the top of the guide; shares up 9% pre-market.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Raised
TAKEAWAYS.text: First 2027 guide, $18.5bn or 38% to 40% growth, sits 14.5% above consensus; AI fabrics double to $7bn.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Watch
TAKEAWAYS.text: Gross margin fell to 64.0% from 65.2% a year ago; 2027 is guided at 62% to 64%.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Valuation
TAKEAWAYS.text: 32.2x forward earnings pre-results, close to the 31.7x average since 2015, after 39.5x over the past year.

H_P1: The 2027 guide lifts the earnings base
P1_PARAGRAPH: Revenue beat consensus by 9.7%, the first 2027 guide sits 14.5% above it, and the shares rose about 9% in pre-market trading on 4 November, the session after the release: surprise and reaction are aligned. Growth accelerated to 58.5% on a $3.66bn base, and management commits to 38% to 40% more in 2027 at a 49% operating margin.
C1_TITLE: ANET: Q3 2026 results and guidance vs. expectations
C1_SUB: Surprise in %, reported or guided vs. pre-results consensus · Q3 EPS vs. the midpoint of the $1.06–1.08 guide · 2026 and 2027 guides at the midpoint
C1_COMMENT: The largest surprise sits in 2027: the $18.5bn guide is 14.5% above the $16.2bn consensus, and management raised its 2026 outlook for the fourth time this year, to $13.3bn. The quarter came with operating leverage: non-GAAP operating income rose 60.1% to $1.80bn, faster than revenue, for a 49.1% margin, against 48.6% a year ago.
BASE_CASE: The $18.5bn 2027 guide sits 14.5% above consensus at a 49% operating margin, and consensus 12-month forward EPS is already up 8.6% to $5.45; another 10% upgrade takes the multiple back to its 31.7x average after the pre-market gain. The case remains very constructive: we underwrite 38% to 40% growth led by AI fabrics at $7bn and campus at $2bn. In our view, the 22% October fall cleared crowded positioning. The next test is the Q4 report in February.
UPSIDE: Q4 revenue above the $4.0bn top of the guide; a third and fourth customer above 10% of revenue; the $11.4bn of purchase commitments shipping with gross margin at 63% or more.
DOWNSIDE: A 2027 gross margin below the 62% floor; inventory, now $3.2bn, rising faster than revenue; a capex cut at one of the large cloud customers or deferred revenue below $6.8bn.
H_A1: Results: AI and enterprise drove the beat
A1_PARAGRAPHS: Product revenue rose 67% year on year to $3.19bn and services 18% to $468m, taking total revenue up 20.5% on the quarter to $3.66bn, with growth led by AI and enterprise customers. Non-GAAP gross margin of 64.0% came in above the 63% guide and 90bp above consensus on a favourable customer and product mix, 120bp below the 65.2% of Q3 2025. Operating expenses rose, yet non-GAAP operating income grew 60.1% to $1.80bn for a 49.1% margin, and EPS rose 56% to $1.20. Arista now counts more than 100 AI customers on its Etherlink platform and expects three to four customers above 10% of revenue in 2026, from two in 2025.

Surprise and reaction point the same way. Revenue beat consensus by 9.7% and EPS cleared the top of the guide by 11%, and the shares rose about 9% in pre-market trading on 4 November from a $169.91 close on 3 November. The confirmed drivers are the 2027 guide, 14.5% above consensus, the fourth raise to the 2026 outlook and purchase commitments of $11.4bn, up from $9.7bn at the end of Q2. The size of the move is consistent with lighter positioning, which we cannot confirm: the stock had fallen 21.6% from its 9 October record of $216.74 and 10.8% since the Q2 results.
H_A2: Outlook: a fourth raise and 38% to 40% next
A2_PARAGRAPH: For Q4, management guides to revenue of $3.9bn to $4.0bn, gross margin of 63% to 64%, an operating margin of 48% to 49% and EPS of $1.26 to $1.30 on 1.28bn shares, which puts 2026 revenue just over $13.3bn, up 48%. The first 2027 guide calls for 38% to 40% growth to $18.5bn, with AI fabrics doubling to about $7bn, campus up 60% to about $2bn, gross margin of 62% to 64% and an operating margin near 49%. Scale-up trials start in 2027 and production in 2028, so the guide excludes material scale-up revenue. Supply is better covered: inventory reached $3.2bn from $2.5bn and the CFO stated confidence in supply.
H_C2: Valuation: earnings outran the share price
C2_TITLE: ANET: share price vs. consensus earnings and valuation
C2_SUB: Weekly, January 2015 to 4 November 2026 · Last price is the 3 November close, before the release; EPS includes the first post-results revisions · Bloomberg 12m-forward consensus · 40-week simple MA · Log scale · P/E shaded above (orange) / below (blue) its 2015–26 average
C2_COMMENT: Consensus 12-month forward EPS rose 66.6% over the past year to $5.45, against 26.2% for the share price, so the forward P/E fell from 41.2x to 32.2x, 1.6% above its 31.7x average since 2015 and well below the 39.5x one-year average. The first post-results revisions lifted EPS 8.6% in a week. The price sits 2.3% above its 40-week moving average of $166.2. After the 9% pre-market gain the multiple is about 35x; a further 10% upgrade at that price brings it back to the long-run average.
SOURCE_LINE: Source: Syz Research, Bloomberg, company filings, Arista Networks release and earnings call of 3 November 2026
